payload.selection_rationale: One proposal (practice) was handed over, and I took its core with three repairs. Against what the survey and spike measured, it holds up. (1) eng/ is PowerShell today, so a dependency-free PowerShell parity check fits. (2) The SL-022 harness matched 16/16 once patched, so porting it is safer than rewriting it. (3) The spike measured that a text diff misses recorded divergences (7 of 12 identical after normalising). That measurement is the reason for two tools rather than one, and the proposal is built around it. The pieces are the smallest set that discharges C1-C4. The one thing beyond the slice text is the caller Fact, which stays because a script nothing runs leaves the header comment as the only guard. Deleting the Fact and its .cs file undoes that piece. I did not pick the spike's suggested route for the clean-clone no-go (reimplement Fitness's semantics with the stdlib, or vendor the engine module). That would be a third copy of the rules' semantics, kept in step with the engine by nothing, which is the problem this slice exists to remove. The parity check has no engine dependency and runs anywhere. The behavioural harness needs the TAAD engine and says so with exit 2. I added three repairs: how the scratch copy gets an SDK, how content pairing behaves when two Facts share a pattern set, and the port-first build order. The 16-versus-17 plant count is reconciled at build against expected.json, not decided here.

components.name: Rule parity check
components.responsibility: Covers C3 and C4 as a script under eng/. Reads tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ArchitectureRulesTests.cs and .taad/fitness.yaml as explicit UTF-8 (LF or CRLF), so it behaves the same under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7. The C# reader finds each [Fact]/[Theory] method and its single AssertNoMatch( call. It accepts only lone verbatim @"..." literals, one per line, ending ',' or ');'. Any other line inside a call block (two literals, wrapping, concatenation, const, nameof, interpolation, raw string) exits 2 with file:line. The YAML reader uses line regexes and no YAML library. It stops at the first '# settled by SL-' comment, so settled entries are neither read nor compared. It accepts only single-quoted pattern scalars ('' decoded to '), and any other quoting exits 2. The normaliser is a closed list. A twinned yaml pattern MUST start with (?m), which is then stripped, because xUnit applies RegexOptions.Multiline to every pattern and a missing (?m) is semantic drift. '^﻿?' (escape in either case, or a literal U+FEFF) is treated as '^'. C# "" is decoded to ". Nothing else is equal. Pairing works on normalised pattern multisets. Group Facts and entries by multiset key. Every Fact needs at least one entry with its key, and every entry above the marker needs a Fact with its key. If two Facts share a key, entries must be at least as many as Facts for that key. Guards against a vacuous pass: at least 1 Fact, at least 1 pattern per Fact, and -ExpectFacts must equal the Fact count when given. Before comparing, it drops one pattern from its own in-memory parse of the first twinned entry and exits 2 if the comparator does not then report drift. Output is ASCII only, with non-ASCII escaped as \uXXXX.
components.key_interactions: Called by RuleCopiesAgreeTests on every test run, and by the harness as its first step. It writes nothing, so it can run inside the person's checkout during `dotnet test` without dirtying it.

components.name: Parity caller
components.responsibility: One [Fact] in its own class. It counts the [Fact]/[Theory] methods on ArchitectureRulesTests by reflection (FactAttribute, inherit: true), which is the runtime count the spike required in place of trusting the extractor's own. It launches `powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File <root>/eng/rules-parity.ps1 -Root <root> -ExpectFacts <n>` through ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList with a 60 s timeout, asserts exit 0, and puts stdout and stderr in the failure message. It finds the repo root with whatever mechanism ArchitectureRulesTests already uses. The class and method names must not contain the substring 'ArchitectureRulesTests', so the harness's FullyQualifiedName~ArchitectureRulesTests filter excludes it and the trx total stays equal to the Fact count.
components.key_interactions: This is what makes C3 true in effect. TAAD's build and validate stages run Core.Tests, so drift fails a gate. It launches a process and parses nothing, so C4 holds. Architecture rule 2 enforces that.

components.name: Planted-violation harness
components.responsibility: Covers C1 and C2. It is a port of %TEMP%\sl022-val3\{setup3.py, analyse3.py} and its DIV3 block, with %TEMP%\sl022-fitness\{divergences.ps1, encodings.ps1} folded in. Usage is `<engine python> eng/rules-harness/harness.py [--root R] [--engine-root E | env TAAD3_BACKEND] [--keep]`. --root defaults to the repo containing the script. No C:\Users\... or sl022-* path survives the port. Its only non-stdlib import is taad3.fitness, reached through one adapter function run_fitness(root) so a CLI swap touches one place. Before any import it sets TAAD3_HOME to a scratch directory and sys.dont_write_bytecode, so nothing is written into taad_v3 and no live ledger is migrated. It probes `import taad3.fitness` and `import yaml`, and exits 2 naming the engine path on failure. Sequence: (1) run rules-parity.ps1 and exit 2 on drift, because behaviour over drifted text is noise. (2) Copy `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard` to tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='fsa-rules-'). (3) Ensure the SDK exists by running the ROOT's eng/dotnet.ps1 (which bootstraps root/.dotnet, gitignored, allowed by Q-003), then build the scratch projects with the root's script pointed at scratch paths. If the script cannot be pointed at another tree, call <root>/.dotnet/dotnet.exe directly. The scratch copy has no .dotnet/ because it is gitignored, so this avoids a 300 MB download per run and any junction whose deletion could follow into the real SDK. (4) For each scenario (clean, plants, divergences): apply rows, run `test --no-build --filter FullyQualifiedName~ArchitectureRulesTests --logger trx`, run run_fitness(scratch), then restore every touched file against a SHA-256 manifest. The clean scenario must give zero hits in both engines, empty unmatched and unran lists, a Fitness rule count equal to the number of yaml entries (derived, replacing the hard-coded 8), and a trx total equal to the parity Fact count. Otherwise exit 2. Hits are attributed to rows by (repo-relative path, case-insensitive; planted line range). The planted line is computed at plant time and never stored. Row verdicts: AS-RECORDED, MISSED-BY-XUNIT, MISSED-BY-FITNESS, FIRED-WHEN-EXEMPT, DIVERGENCE-CLOSED, STRAY-HIT, PLANT-BROKEN (target missing, or planted text absent after planting). It prints an ASCII-only matrix (stdout is cp1252 on this machine) and reads every file as UTF-8. It deletes the scratch copy on success, keeps it on failure and prints its path. It asserts that `git status --porcelain` of --root is unchanged.
components.key_interactions: Reads plants.json and divergences.json. Runs the parity script, the repo's eng/dotnet.ps1 (pwsh if present, else powershell.exe) and xUnit. Imports taad3.fitness from the engine root. Never reimplements Fitness's glob, skip-dir, size or encoding semantics. Architecture rule 3 enforces that.

components.name: Plant rows
components.responsibility: Hand-kept rows: {id, rule, file, op: new-file|append|insert-after, anchor?, text, expect:{xunit: fire|quiet, fitness: fire|quiet}}. The set is the 16 must-fire plants recorded in sl022-val3's expected.json (the set the spike re-ran 16/16), plus the must-not-fire exempt-file rows P07c-e from sl022-fitness\plants.ps1 that are not already among them, deduplicated by (file, text). Each scope of the three Facts split across two scopes has its own plant. A top-level _note gives the reconciled counts (N must-fire, M must-not-fire) and says where the 16-versus-17 difference went. It cites SL-022 by id and never by %TEMP% path. Expected outcomes come from SL-022's recorded outputs and are changed only by a person.
components.key_interactions: Read by harness.py. Edited by a person when a rule is added, removed or rescoped.

components.name: Divergence rows
components.responsibility: The 12 recorded divergences (from SL-022's divergences.json, encodings.json and analyse3.out.txt) as rows D1..Dn. They use the plant ops plus create-with {encoding: utf16le|cp1252|utf8bom, pad_to_bytes} and rename-case (a two-step rename through a temp name, so it is a real case change on NTFS). They cover files under packages/ and dist/, EntryClassifier.cs to Entryclassifier.cs, TestNative.cs to testNative.cs, the using split across two lines (D5), UTF-16 and non-UTF-8 files, and a file over 2 MB. Each row carries the per-engine outcome SL-022 recorded. Rows are strict: when both engines now agree on one, the harness reports DIVERGENCE-CLOSED and exits 1, telling the person to delete the row and its line in the yaml header.
components.key_interactions: Rows correspond one-to-one with the prose list at .taad/fitness.yaml:21-34, which gains the same D-ids.

components.name: fitness.yaml header
components.responsibility: A comment-only edit to lines 1-61. Replace 'kept in step by this comment' with: the check is eng/rules-parity.ps1, run by RuleCopiesAgreeTests; twinned patterns are single-quoted and start with (?m); '^﻿?' is allowed; twinned entries go above the first '# settled by' line and engine-appended rules go below it; when a rule changes, run eng/rules-harness/harness.py (needs the TAAD engine). Tag the divergence list at lines 21-34 with D-ids. No key is added to any entry, because the engine refuses a key no rule reads (taad_v3 f58b2aa).
components.key_interactions: Parsed by the TAAD Fitness engine (comments ignored) and by rules-parity.ps1 (which relies on the marker comment surviving).

components.name: ArchitectureRulesTests format note
components.responsibility: One comment line above the class: patterns are one verbatim literal per line, and eng/rules-parity.ps1 reads them against .taad/fitness.yaml. No behaviour change.
components.key_interactions: Tells whoever reformats the file why RuleCopiesAgreeTests will refuse it.

contracts.name: eng/rules-parity.ps1
contracts.auth_model: None: a local script run as the ordinary user; it reads two files and writes nothing.
contracts.error_cases: exit 0: AGREE. exit 1: DRIFT, followed by up to 10 lines, each naming the yaml entry and its line, the nearest Fact, and the differing normalised pattern. exit 2: CANNOT-READ (file missing; an unclassifiable line in a call block; a non-single-quoted yaml pattern; zero Facts or patterns; a Fact count that differs from -ExpectFacts; a self-mutation that failed to produce DRIFT). Not being able to check never reads as agreement.
contracts.notes: Args: -Root <repo> (default: the parent of the script directory), -ExpectFacts <int> (optional). The first stdout line is the verdict, e.g. 'rules-parity: AGREE 7 facts <- 10 twinned entries, 21 patterns; 4 settled entries not compared (patterns only; engine behaviour is rules-harness)'. The exit-code and terse-summary contract follows the cited leondixon/harness fitness-function contract. It compares patterns only: a scope or exemption dropped from one copy is invisible to it and is the harness's job.

contracts.name: eng/rules-harness/harness.py
contracts.auth_model: None: local, ordinary user. It needs the TAAD engine checkout and that engine's interpreter, and never the shared ~/.claude venv.
contracts.error_cases: exit 0: every row AS-RECORDED. exit 1: at least one row MISSED-BY-XUNIT, MISSED-BY-FITNESS, FIRED-WHEN-EXEMPT, DIVERGENCE-CLOSED, STRAY-HIT or PLANT-BROKEN. exit 2: cannot measure (engine not importable or its result missing a field; parity drift; build failed; clean baseline not clean; unran or unmatched rules on clean; trx total differs from the parity Fact count; restore hash mismatch; git status of --root changed).
contracts.notes: Leaves `git status --porcelain` of --root unchanged. The repo-local .dotnet/ it may create is gitignored and allowed by Q-003. Not a routine test: it costs a build and needs taad_v3, so it is run when a rule changes and by the build node that discharges C1/C2.

contracts.name: Plant and divergence row schema
contracts.error_cases: An unknown op, or a missing target for append, insert-after or rename-case, is PLANT-BROKEN (exit 1), never a silent no-op. A row missing an expect key exits 2.
contracts.notes: The files are data, so a change to an expected outcome shows as a reviewable diff. Nothing writes expect from a run.

contracts.name: RuleCopiesAgreeTests (the single Fact)
contracts.error_cases: Fails on a non-zero exit or a 60 s timeout, with the script's output in the assertion message.
contracts.notes: The only permanent caller of the parity check. Runs in the ordinary Core.Tests suite; excluded from harness runs by the ArchitectureRulesTests filter.

contracts.name: taad3.fitness.check(root) (external, consumed)
contracts.auth_model: In-process import from --engine-root, with TAAD3_HOME pointed at scratch before the import.
contracts.error_cases: An import failure, a changed signature or a missing result field gives exit 2 naming the engine path. It is never reported as the engine disagreeing.
contracts.notes: The survey measured the result shape today through %TEMP%\sl022-fitness\fit.py: verdict, rule count, files read, unmatched, unran, violations. The build may switch run_fitness() to a taad_v3 CLI if f58b2aa exposes one that emits machine-readable output.

key_decisions.decision: Two tools, split by cost and by what each can see. A text parity check (PowerShell, no dependencies, run on every test run through one Fact) guards pattern drift. A behavioural harness (dotnet plus the TAAD engine, run by hand or by a build node when a rule changes) guards engine semantics, scope and exemption drift, and pins the known divergences.
key_decisions.rationale: The spike measured that text agreement alone misses recorded divergences: 7 of 12 have identical pattern text after normalising, and all 12 read identical once '﻿?' is allowed. The harness alone costs a build and needs the engine, so nobody would run it routinely.

key_decisions.decision: The harness measures the real Fitness engine, imported from an explicit --engine-root / TAAD3_BACKEND. It does not reimplement or vendor Fitness's glob, SKIP_DIRS, 2 MB and UTF-8 semantics. It therefore cannot run from a clean clone without TAAD. The spike's no-go on harness-runs-from-clean-clone is accepted as true of this design, not worked around.
key_decisions.rationale: A reimplementation would be a third copy of the rules' semantics, kept in step with the engine by nothing, so it pins the copy and stays green while the real gate changes. Making the dependency explicit (a parameter, a probe, exit 2) replaces the hard-coded sys.path that broke SL-022's scripts. The check that must run everywhere (parity) has no such dependency. The cost falls only on the harness; vendoring later is a rewrite of that one file.

key_decisions.decision: Parity compares patterns only, pairs entries to Facts by normalised pattern-multiset content with no twin-name map, and stops at the first '# settled by SL-' comment. Scope and exemption parity is left to the harness. The known blind spot is one of two scope entries of a split Fact deleted from yaml, which parity reports as AGREE. It is covered by the per-scope plant rows.
key_decisions.rationale: The spike measured that twins are equal after the (?m)/BOM-guard strip and that split Facts duplicate their whole pattern list across 2 scopes (30 twinned yaml patterns = 21 + 9). Content pairing works today and needs no third file. Mapping C# Files/StartsWith/Except to globs is the separate translation layer the spike warned about.

key_decisions.decision: The normaliser is exactly the header's authoring rules and nothing else: (?m) required and stripped; '^﻿?' equals '^'; verbatim "" and single-quoted '' decoded. Both readers fail closed on any shape they cannot classify, and the Fact count is checked against runtime reflection.
key_decisions.rationale: Requiring (?m) rather than stripping it only if present catches real semantic drift: Python '^' without MULTILINE anchors only at the file start, where xUnit's Multiline anchors every line. Fail-closed classification plus a reflected Fact count meets the spike's constraint (fail on non-lone lines, check the count against a runtime count) without instrumenting AssertNoMatch.

key_decisions.decision: The parity check has a permanent caller: one [Fact] in a new RuleCopiesAgreeTests.cs that shells out to powershell.exe and passes the reflected Fact count. It launches and parses nothing.
key_decisions.rationale: A script under eng/ that nothing runs leaves the header comment as the only guard (an endpoint with no caller). TAAD's stages already run Core.Tests, so this is the one automatic caller the project has. powershell.exe is used because it exists on every Windows 10/11 install and pwsh may not. C4 holds because no parser lives in .NET. This is the one element beyond the slice's own text; see open question 1.

key_decisions.decision: Divergence rows are strict: a pinned divergence that both engines now agree on fails as DIVERGENCE-CLOSED, just as a new disagreement fails.
key_decisions.rationale: Without strictness the known-divergence list rots in one direction, and the prose at fitness.yaml:21-34 becomes false with nothing noticing. That is the same failure as the header comment this slice replaces (pytest xfail(strict=True) transfer).

key_decisions.decision: Expected outcomes are ported from SL-022's recorded outputs and changed only by hand. The planted line is computed when a row is applied and never stored. A clean scenario with zero hits and STRAY-HIT detection bracket every run.
key_decisions.rationale: Stored line numbers already rotted once: the spike found the expected-hit list needed a new SL-024 hit at Scanner.cs:11. Regenerating expectations from a run turns the harness into a recorder that always agrees. With the clean control and stray-hit detection, a hit nobody planted cannot be absorbed into the matrix.

key_decisions.decision: Building and planting happen in a %TEMP% scratch copy made from `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard` and built once. The SDK comes from the ROOT's eng/dotnet.ps1 (root/.dotnet), which is invoked against scratch paths, with a direct <root>/.dotnet/dotnet.exe fallback. Scenarios are applied in place with `--no-build` and undone against a SHA-256 manifest.
key_decisions.rationale: This repairs a gap in the proposal. .dotnet/ is gitignored, so a scratch copy would have no SDK and would re-download 300 MB per run on a machine that has only SDK 8 and 9. Using the root's SDK avoids that without a junction, which a recursive scratch cleanup could follow into the real SDK. `--no-build` means planted lines never have to compile. Planting in the one built copy works whether ArchitectureRulesTests finds its root at runtime or through [CallerFilePath] (nobody has checked which). Copying the working tree rather than HEAD measures the edit the person is about to commit.

key_decisions.decision: The harness is Python, run under the TAAD engine's own interpreter, and the parity check is PowerShell 5.1/7-compatible. No Python project, requirements file or venv is added to this repo. The project's stack block does not name Python, so this choice is declared in stack_chosen.
key_decisions.rationale: The harness needs the engine's interpreter anyway to import taad3.fitness (which lazily imports yaml). Porting analyse3/setup3, which matched 16/16 once patched, is cheaper and safer than rewriting them in PowerShell. The parity check must run where only Windows exists, and eng/ is PowerShell today.

key_decisions.decision: Build order: first copy the still-present sources out of %TEMP%\sl022-fitness and %TEMP%\sl022-val3 into the worktree (Test-Path each; Storage Sense state was not read). If they are gone, raise an obligation naming the risk-spike stage rather than reconstructing plants from memory. Then build parity, the Fact, the harness and the header edit. Prove each guard bites by putting the defect back: a typo in one copy fails the Fact, and a removed rule scope shows MISSED-BY-*. The port drops SL-022's engine-side controls (append.py, the `design` import, ctl-noyaml), because Q-009 put design._append_rules in taad_v3, outside this project.
key_decisions.rationale: The spike's sl022-harness-still-in-temp verdict was conditional on the OS not cleaning %TEMP%. A guard that passes without ever having failed proves nothing.

proposals.note: The only proposal. Its core was taken whole: two tools, the Fact caller, the strict divergence rows, and the real-engine dependency accepted against the spike's clean-clone no-go. Repairs: the scratch copy's SDK source, pairing when two Facts share a pattern set, port-first build order, and open questions on the Fact and on the engine dependency.

payload.coherence_check:
One proposal, so there is no composition across designers to check. Nothing here has survived a disagreement, and the reviewer should argue with it first. The least-contested choices are the harness depending on the outside TAAD engine, the shelling Fact in Core.Tests, and strict divergence rows.

I checked the proposal's internal seams instead.

(a) Parity and the harness share one definition of 'agree'. The harness runs the parity script first and exits 2 on drift, so behavioural rows are never measured over drifted text.

(b) The rules this design declares in architecture_rules are appended by the engine as settled entries below the '# settled by' marker. They have no xUnit twin, as the four existing settled entries have none. That is consistent with parity stopping at the marker. They must not be authored above it, and the header edit says so. If the engine ever stops writing the marker, settled entries read as twinned and surface loudly as unpaired (DRIFT), not silently.

(c) The Fact's class and method names avoid the substring 'ArchitectureRulesTests', so the harness's FullyQualifiedName~ArchitectureRulesTests filter excludes it. That keeps the harness's trx total equal to the parity Fact count, which is a clean-scenario check.

(d) I redesigned one seam. The proposal built in a scratch copy through the repo's eng/dotnet.ps1, but .dotnet/ is gitignored and absent from a `git ls-files` copy. Each run would re-download a 300 MB SDK on a machine with only SDK 8 and 9. The design now uses the root's SDK against scratch paths and keeps no junction, so cleanup cannot delete the real SDK.

(e) The spike's two no-gos are consumed, not waved off. The no-go on text agreement is why there are two tools. The no-go on the clean clone is accepted as true of the harness and false of the parity check, and the design says so instead of building a reimplemented engine.

(f) Known blind spot: one of two scope entries of a split Fact deleted from yaml is invisible to parity. The per-scope plant rows are the only guard, so plants.json must keep one plant per scope.

(g) Engine reachability is unresolved. Whether the nodes that must discharge C1/C2 can reach the taad_v3 path under the machine boundary was not measured. If they cannot, only the engine half of the harness falls to a person to run. The parity check and the Fact still discharge C3/C4.

(h) The three architecture rules apply to files that exist only after build. Before then, Fitness would list them unmatched, which is expected.

Cross-domain transfer: pytest xfail(strict=True), carried from the proposal into the strict divergence rows.

architecture_rules.name: eng tooling carries no machine-specific path
architecture_rules.because: The SL-022 harness crashed from a clean clone on exactly these: C:\Users\sshub\... constants and %TEMP%\sl022-* trees. A check pinned to one machine's path cannot run in another worktree or checkout, and it fails silently as 'cannot measure'. Cite SL-022 by id in notes, never by path. The two pre-existing scripts are excepted because this design does not govern them.

architecture_rules.name: the .NET caller launches the check and parses nothing
architecture_rules.because: The slice's design rejected a rule parser inside the .NET project as over-built (C4). A third reader of the two rule copies would itself need keeping in step with them, which is the drift this slice exists to remove. The Fact may only launch eng/rules-parity.ps1 and assert its exit code.

architecture_rules.name: the harness measures the real Fitness engine and never a copy of it
architecture_rules.because: A reimplemented matcher or a private YAML reader pins the copy. The harness would stay green while the engine's glob, skip-dir, size or encoding behaviour changed, which is exactly the divergence class this slice measures. Only taad3.fitness may read fitness.yaml.

cases.behaviour: check that the two rule copies agree
cases.shape: the clean tree: 7 Facts, 10 twinned yaml entries, 21 patterns, 4 settled entries below the marker
cases.why: The baseline every other row is measured against. A checker that cannot say AGREE here is broken, and one that says it by skipping is vacuous. Run it under both powershell.exe 5.1 (the Fact's shell) and pwsh 7 (the harness's), since file decoding differs between them.

cases.behaviour: check that the two rule copies agree
cases.shape: a pattern is edited or dropped in only one copy (a typo in yaml, or one of a Fact's five patterns missing from its twin)
cases.why: This is the drift the header comment claimed to prevent. Pairing is by pattern multiset, so a changed pattern must show as an unpaired entry and an unpaired Fact, naming both with file:line.

cases.behaviour: check that the two rule copies agree
cases.shape: a Fact with no yaml entry, or a yaml entry above the settled marker with no Fact (a deleted twin, or a new rule authored in the wrong place)
cases.why: The pairing branch. Three Facts carry two scope entries each, so 'at least one entry per Fact' must not be satisfied by a stale one. Rules the engine appended below the marker must stay ignored.

cases.shape: a twinned yaml pattern that lacks (?m), or spells the BOM guard as ﻿ in upper case, lower case, or a literal U+FEFF
cases.why: Without (?m), Python '^' anchors only at the file start while xUnit's Multiline anchors every line. That is semantic drift that text equality would hide. The three BOM spellings must equal '^' or the clean tree reads as drifted (measured: 0 of 21 match without the strip).

cases.shape: a shape the reader cannot classify or count: two literals on one C# line, concatenation, raw string, const or nameof, a Fact with no AssertNoMatch or zero patterns, a double-quoted or block YAML pattern, zero Facts, or a Fact count differing from the reflected count
cases.why: The failure mode is silence: a pattern the line regex misses is a pattern nobody compares. It must exit 2 with file:line and never AGREE (spike constraint: fail on non-lone lines, check the count against a runtime count).

cases.shape: the engine root is missing, wrong, or taad3.fitness imports but its result lacks a field
cases.why: It must exit 2 naming the path and never report the engine as disagreeing. TAAD3_HOME must already point at scratch before the import, because importing taad3 opens a Store that migrates whatever it points at.

The baseline and the STRAY-HIT bracket. It must give zero hits in both engines, empty unmatched and unran, a Fitness rule count equal to the yaml entry count (derived; 14 today, not the hard-coded 8), and a trx total equal to the Fact count (7). Otherwise a hit nobody planted, like the SL-024 one at Scanner.cs:11, is absorbed.

cases.behaviour: plant a violation the rules must catch
cases.shape: the 16 must-fire plants, including one per scope of each of the 3 Facts split across two scopes, with insert-after rows landing in files that already have lines
cases.why: One plant per scope is the only thing that catches a scope deleted from one copy (parity's blind spot). Attribution is by path and computed planted line range, because stored lines rotted once.

cases.behaviour: plant a violation in an exempted file
cases.why: Exemptions use different notation in the two copies (C# Except versus yaml except_files). A dropped exemption shows only here, as FIRED-WHEN-EXEMPT.

cases.behaviour: scan a file the engines walk differently
cases.shape: a violating file under packages/ or under dist/ (D1, D2)
cases.why: SKIP_DIRS lives inside the Fitness engine, so xUnit fires and Fitness stays quiet. The row pins the real engine's behaviour, not a copy of it.

cases.behaviour: scan a file the engines read differently
cases.shape: UTF-16LE, cp1252 (non-UTF-8), and a file over 2 MB, each carrying a violation
cases.why: Fitness decodes UTF-8 and applies a 2 MB limit. xUnit does not, so each shape has a recorded per-engine outcome that a silent engine change would flip.

cases.shape: a case-only rename of an exempted file (EntryClassifier.cs to Entryclassifier.cs, TestNative.cs to testNative.cs), done as a two-step rename through a temp name on NTFS
cases.why: One engine matches the exemption case-sensitively and the other does not (D3, D4). A one-step rename can be a no-op, and the shape only exists on a case-preserving filesystem.

cases.shape: the using split across two lines (D5)
cases.why: Whether a line-scoped regex or a multiline match sees it differs between the engines. This is a recorded divergence with identical pattern text on both sides, so parity cannot see it.

cases.shape: a recorded divergence that both engines now agree on
cases.why: Strict rows must exit 1 as DIVERGENCE-CLOSED. Otherwise the prose list at fitness.yaml:21-34 outlives the behaviour it describes.

stack_chosen.choice: PowerShell (Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh 7 compatible) for eng/rules-parity.ps1. Python 3, stdlib plus taad3.fitness only, for eng/rules-harness/harness.py.
stack_chosen.why: The project stack block names C# only. The eng/ scripts are PowerShell, so the check that must run anywhere stays PowerShell. The harness has to import taad3.fitness, so it is Python. Later slices touching eng/ inherit this split. Python is not a project runtime, and nothing under src/ or tests/ uses it.

stack_chosen.choice: The harness runs under the TAAD engine's own interpreter, passed by the caller. No requirements.txt, pyproject or venv is added to this repo, and the shared ~/.claude venv is never used.
stack_chosen.why: The engine's interpreter already has the dependencies that taad3.fitness lazily imports (yaml). A repo venv would be a second dependency set that nothing else in this C# project needs.

stack_chosen.choice: Plant and divergence rows are JSON data files. xUnit results are read through the trx logger. The single new Fact lives in the existing Core.Tests project. No new test framework or project.
stack_chosen.why: Data files make an expected-outcome change a reviewable diff. The trx logger gives a machine-readable total for the clean-baseline check. The existing xUnit project is the only automatic caller TAAD's gates already run.

cross_domain_transfer.pattern: xfail(strict=True): a test marked as an expected failure that starts passing is itself reported as a failure, so the list of known failures cannot silently outlive them.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: The divergence rows are a list of known failures, each a place where xUnit and Fitness are recorded as disagreeing, documented in prose at fitness.yaml:21-34. Non-strict expected-failure lists only grow: a fix lands, the marker stays, and the document lies. Applied here, an engine change that closes a divergence forces deletion of the row and its header line in the same change.

invariants.precondition: Each divergence outcome is deterministic from run to run (strict mode on a flaky case produces noise, not signal).
invariants.evidence: Each shape should depend only on file bytes, size, directory name, path case or line split, and SL-022 recorded each outcome once. The build should run the divergences scenario twice and require identical verdicts.

invariants.precondition: The scratch copy is on a case-preserving filesystem, so the case-only rename rows (D3, D4) actually change the name.
invariants.evidence: %TEMP% is on NTFS on this machine. The harness should assert that the on-disk name after the two-step rename differs in case from the original before trusting the row.

invariants.precondition: A closed divergence is caught by exit code, not by a person reading the matrix.
invariants.evidence: Not yet built. Build should temporarily flip one row's recorded outcome and confirm the harness exits 1 with DIVERGENCE-CLOSED.

prior_art.pattern: Fitness-function contract: an executable check that exits 0 on pass and non-zero on violation, with a short violation summary whose first line names the verdict.
Prove an architecture rule both passes on the real tree and fires when deliberately violated, with the checker generic over a root argument so fixtures can be synthetic trees.
Clean/planted twin: one copy must pass and the planted copy must fail with an explicit marker, run on every commit as standing proof that each check catches what it claims.
pytest xfail(strict=True): an expected failure that starts passing is reported as a failure.
prior_art.where: pytest documentation, 'strict' parameter of the xfail marker

decidable_disagreements.question: Can the harness reach the real Fitness engine from inside the build and validate nodes that must discharge C1/C2, or must the engine half be reimplemented or vendored in the repo so a node without access to the taad_v3 path can still run it?
decidable_disagreements.positions: The practice proposal: import taad3.fitness from an explicit --engine-root, accepting that the harness cannot run from a clean clone. The spike (harness-runs-from-clean-clone, no-go, needs-first): apply Fitness's glob, skip-dir, 2 MB, encoding and regex semantics with the stdlib only, or vendor a pinned copy of the engine's fitness module. Reality decides the reachability half: run the harness once from a build node, with the machine boundary's guard active. The vendoring half is a design and taste question, decided against it above because a copy pins the copy.

taste_disagreements: Parity in PowerShell and the harness in Python (two languages under eng/), versus one language for both. Python for the parity check would make every test run depend on an interpreter the platform constraint cannot assume; PowerShell for the harness would need a Python bridge to taad3 anyway.

A shelling Fact in Core.Tests as the permanent caller, versus a script-only check that someone must remember to run. The slice text says 'lives under eng/ as a script'; the Fact is the one addition beyond it.
Pairing entries to Facts by pattern content, versus an explicit twin-name map. Content pairing needs no third file but cannot see a scope entry dropped from one of a split Fact's two.
Plants and divergences as JSON data files beside harness.py, versus inline literals in the script.
The name and location eng/rules-harness/ with harness.py, plants.json and divergences.json, versus a flat eng/ layout or a single README-documented script.
Tagging the divergence prose at fitness.yaml:21-34 with D-ids, versus leaving the header prose as the SL-022 author wrote it.
open_questions: Does the person want the parity check wired into the test suite (RuleCopiesAgreeTests launches powershell.exe on every `dotnet test`), or left as a script under eng/ that someone must remember to run? The design wires it, so drift fails a gate instead of depending on memory. Deleting that one file reverses it, at the cost of the header comment being the only automatic guard again.

Is it acceptable that the behavioural harness (C1/C2) runs only where the TAAD engine checkout exists and is never part of a routine test run? It is kept in the repo and cannot run from a clean clone. Only the parity check (C3) runs anywhere.
